text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and finding the pagination code.
The bug is visible at line 31: `end = start + page_size - 1` is used as the slice end, which is inclusive-style, so the slice drops one item per page. Let me view the full file to confirm.

Confirmed: `items[start:end]` with `end = start + page_size - 1` returns only `page_size - 1` items per page, so the item at each page boundary (positions 5, 10, ...) is never returned. The fix is to make the slice end `start + page_size`.
All 29 tests pass. Let me finish.

args.summary: Fixed off-by-one in library/pagination.py's paginate(). The slice end was computed as `start + page_size - 1`, so each page returned only page_size-1 items and the item at every page boundary (positions 5, 10, ... for page size 5) was silently dropped. Changed the end to `start + page_size`, so each page returns exactly page_size items (the last page is still truncated naturally by the list slice). With 11 SKUs and page size 5, all 11 are now returned across the 3 pages. The full test suite passes (29/29); no test files were modified.
